how_the_queue_was_reconstructed.why_it_mattered: Governance and the instruction disagreed on three items, and in every case the repository was right. QB1_F#q23 is not a member of the PR1C family at all. The QB10_B free-fall row is a true amendment stated backwards, not a fabrication. RC-10 to RC-12 do not exist. Had the instruction's list been worked directly, one card would have been edited for a defect it does not have, one true amendment would have been deleted as invented, and three phantom items would have been hunted.

dispositions.detail: K-ITEM-P1-LSA-LOWERING-SPEED is discharged. MSC.554(108) was retrieved and read: LSA 6.1.2.8 as amended keeps S = 0.4 + 0.02H and caps it at 1.0 m/s 'whichever is less', and 6.1.2.10 sets 1.3 m/s as an Administration-variable maximum. The card's claim that the range REPLACED the formula is contradicted by the instrument. Pass 1 was right to refuse to guess: both of the card's numbers were real and only the verb was false, so any adjudication from the numbers alone would have confirmed the defect.

dispositions.instruction_ref: section 10 - listed among 'known prior concerns' as a 'false free-fall / 5-knot / 20,000-GT proposition'
dispositions.detail: The proposition is not false. MSC.482(103), adopted 13 May 2021 and in force 1 January 2024, replaced SOLAS III/33.2 to read 'On cargo ships of 20,000 gross tonnage and upwards, davit-launched lifeboats shall be capable of being launched, utilizing painters where necessary, with the ship making headway at speeds up to 5 knots in calm water.' The card was right about the date and the instrument family and wrong about the DIRECTION - the requirement was narrowed to davit-launched lifeboats rather than removed - and about the population, which is cargo ships. Corrected accordingly. Deleting the row as fabricated would have removed a real amendment from a currency card.

2M ended January 2025; THE Alliance became Premier Alliance February 2025 after Hapag-Lloyd left for Gemini. CBER 906/2009 expired 25 April 2024. Three unsupported BAF claims removed. The Pass-1 blocker - 'no primary instrument governs it' - was correct and is precisely why this card decayed unseen: a commercial roster carries no resolution number for a currentness detector to date-check.

Beyond the fabricated anecdote and the MLC misattribution the instruction anticipated, the Numbers to Memorise block had lost both of its numbers from the markup - the 1943 and the 5 were absent from the source, not merely mis-rendered, four lines below a CE-failures bullet warning the candidate not to forget the year.

Membership is twelve. The card taught eleven in its 15-second answer, its 60-second answer and its CE Oral Tip, hedged '11 or 12 depending on', and had dropped KR from the 60-second list - while its own detail list below already enumerated all twelve including KR. The decisive evidence was internal self-contradiction. Note the authority downgrade recorded in the manifest: iacs.org.uk returned HTTP 403 to this session, so the issuer's own page was NOT read and the record says so.

All four distinctions section 5 required are now taught, against PR1C Rev.7 read this pass. The card was worse than the family description: the instrument cited as governing the whole answer, IACS UR Z15, is Hull, Structure, Equipment and Machinery Surveys of Mobile Offshore Drilling Units. It appeared in the Regulatory References box and again in Numbers & Regs.

dispositions.item: Unescaped '<' before a numeral - CLAIMED AS A NEW P1 CLASS, WITHDRAWN
dispositions.detail: The first Pass-2 report named this as remaining P1 debt at five enumerated sites. It is not a defect at any of them. A browser emits '<' literally unless the next character is an ASCII letter, so '<0.01%', '<0.5 m', '<30 m', '<75 dB(A)' and '<130 RPM' all render correctly, as does the '<150 GT' that started this. Verified in a real browser. The escaping applied to QB10_B#q1 is kept as correct markup hygiene and nothing more.
dispositions.the_real_mechanism: '<' followed by an ASCII letter that is not an element name DOES discard text to the next '>'. A census of all 224 pages found 75 distinct tag-like names, every one a real HTML or SVG element. ZERO sites of the damaging form exist in this corpus.

findings.finding: The card published a FALSE claim about its own history in a candidate-facing version stamp, and the manifest recorded it as an invariant: that an unescaped '<' had been deleting about 150 characters of rendered teaching including two entry-into-force dates.
findings.adjudication: UPHELD. HTML5 emits '<' as a literal character unless the next character is an ASCII letter, so '(e.g. <150 GT' always rendered correctly. Verified independently by serving the pre-fix string over HTTP and reading the rendered text back from a real browser: the passage returned complete, both dates present. The same probe confirmed the form that DOES eat text - '<' plus a letter, unclosed.
findings.root_cause: The toolchain's regex tag-stripper models '<' + ANY character as tag-opening. It deleted the text itself and I read its output as evidence about a browser.
findings.closed_by: 5de0c08 / a2f0ca7 - claim withdrawn from card, record and trap; known_traps 126 rewritten; the gate check replaced with one that tests element names against a real list

not_upheld.pr1c_rev7_primary_claim: The reviewer challenged CORR-PASS2-PR1C-SUSPENSION's PRIMARY-on-Rev.7 claim because iacs.org.uk returned 403 and they could obtain only Rev.6. The challenge was well founded on their evidence and the claim is nonetheless correct: Rev.7 was retrieved this pass from IACS's own S3 bucket and read in full, including clause 8 'Rev.7 of this Procedural Requirement applies from 1 January 2026'. The record now carries both S3 URLs and the user-agent condition, so the retrieval is reproducible rather than merely asserted. This is a REPRODUCIBILITY defect in the record, not a truth defect in the claim.
